name: Walnut Creek
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Walnut Creek, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Walnut Creek, CA: Walnut Creek on Ice, Santa at Broadway Plaza, a model train show, Lesher Center holiday shows and garden lights.
lede: Walnut Creek packs a lot of Christmas into a small downtown: an outdoor ice rink with an ice slide in Civic Park, Santa at Broadway Plaza, family holiday shows at the Lesher Center and a giant model railroad in Larkey Park.
celebrates: Downtown Walnut Creek is the center of the season. Walnut Creek Downtown, the downtown business association, sets up Walnut Creek on Ice in Civic Park each year, with an outdoor rink and a tall ice slide, and the city lights its holiday tree in the same park. A few blocks away, Broadway Plaza brings Santa to his workshop and holds a parade of lights. The Lesher Center for the Arts, run by the city, fills December with ballet, concerts and children's plays. At the edge of town, the Ruth Bancroft Garden glows on select nights, and the Walnut Creek Model Railroad Society opens its layout to visitors.
lastyear: In 2025 the city's Annual Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony took place on Friday, November 21, from 5:30 to 6:30 pm in Civic Park at 1375 Civic Drive. Walnut Creek Downtown listed it as free and open to the public, with a meet and greet with Frosty the Snowman to mark opening night of Walnut Creek on Ice a few steps away. Broadway Plaza held its Holiday Parade of Lights and Tree Lighting on Thursday, December 4, 2025, with Santa lighting the tree after the parade.
facts: Walnut Creek takes its name from the Arroyo de las Nueces, Spanish for walnut creek, after the native walnut trees that grew along the water. Early American settlers called the crossroads here The Corners, where the roads from Pacheco and Lafayette met; that spot is now the corner of Mt. Diablo Boulevard and North Main Street. On October 21, 1914, Walnut Creek became the eighth city in Contra Costa County.
trains: Trains helped Walnut Creek grow. The Southern Pacific Railroad arrived in 1891 and cut travel time to the rest of the Bay Area, and the Sacramento Northern Railway's electric line also had a station in town. The Southern Pacific branch ran until the late 1970s, and much of its route is now the Iron Horse Regional Trail. Today BART stops at Walnut Creek station near downtown, Pleasant Hill/Contra Costa Centre station sits just north, and Amtrak's Capitol Corridor stops in nearby Martinez.

kidfact: Walnut Creek is named after a creek, and the creek is named after walnut trees. Long ago the Spanish called it Arroyo de las Nueces, which means creek of the walnuts.
faq: Where is the ice rink in Walnut Creek?

Walnut Creek on Ice is in Civic Park at 1365 Civic Drive, next to downtown. Walnut Creek Downtown runs it each winter, and it has an outdoor rink plus Frosty's Summit, a 90 foot ice slide. Sessions last 90 minutes and tickets are sold online on the rink's ticket site, which is cashless.
Where can kids see Santa in Walnut Creek?

Broadway Plaza sets up Santa's Workshop near True Food Kitchen each holiday season, and the center says visiting Santa is free, with photo packages for sale. The Lesher Center also hosts Visit to the North Pole, a short private Santa visit run by Fantasy Forum Actors Ensemble, and Walnut Creek on Ice has held Santa skate sessions for little ones.
Is there a model train show in Walnut Creek?

Yes. The Walnut Creek Model Railroad Society runs the Diablo Valley Lines, a large HO scale layout in a clubhouse in Larkey Park on Buena Vista Avenue. The club opens it to the public for scheduled shows, including Thanksgiving weekend, and posts its yearly show schedule and small admission fees on its own website.
Can we take BART to Christmas events in Walnut Creek?

Yes. Walnut Creek BART station sits at the north end of downtown, within walking distance of Broadway Plaza and Civic Park. The Ruth Bancroft Garden says its Garden of D'Lights is about 1.5 miles from Pleasant Hill/Contra Costa Centre BART, the next stop north.
What holiday shows are at the Lesher Center?

The Lesher Center for the Arts on Civic Drive hosts several family holiday shows each December, from local ballet productions to Center REP's A Christmas Carol and short plays for young children by Fantasy Forum Actors Ensemble. Each show sells tickets through the Lesher Center box office, and running times and age advice appear on each event page.
